content.value_statement: WordPress Abilities API work can fail when hooks, REST exposure, or permissions are incomplete. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through registration, client use, and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use WordPress 6.9 and later Abilities API features.
Guides category and ability registration with correct initialization hooks.
Documents REST visibility checks for wp-abilities/v1 endpoints.
Recommends input and output schemas for validated agent interactions.
Lists debugging checks for missing abilities and category mismatches.
limitations: Requires an existing WordPress project and target version context.
Does not install WordPress, plugins, or build dependencies by itself.
Cannot verify runtime behavior without a configured WordPress environment.
Version-specific guidance may need confirmation for projects below WordPress 6.9.

use_cases.title: Add Plugin Abilities
use_cases.description: Plan and implement ability categories, callbacks, schemas, REST exposure, and permissions for a WordPress plugin.

use_cases.title: Review Core Integration
use_cases.description: Check hook order, version support, registration timing, and tests for WordPress core Abilities API changes.

use_cases.title: Connect Client Features
use_cases.description: Use @wordpress/abilities to discover exposed abilities and gate JavaScript user interface behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Find Existing Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WordPress project for Abilities API usage. Identify existing registrations, REST endpoints, client usage, and missing setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Register A Read-Only Ability
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a read-only WordPress ability for this plugin. Use the correct category hook, ability hook, stable ID, schemas, and REST visibility.

prompt_templates.title: Debug REST Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: An ability is registered but does not appear in REST responses. Check hook order, category registration, show_in_rest, namespace, and version requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Full Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Abilities API integration for this feature. Include PHP registration, permission callbacks, schemas, REST validation, JavaScript consumption, and focused tests.

output_examples.input: Plan a new read-only ability for a plugin settings summary.
output_examples.output: A registration plan that names the category, ability, input and output expectations, REST visibility, permission checks, and focused tests.

output_examples.input: Debug why a registered ability is not visible to the client.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering hook timing, category presence, REST namespace, visibility settings, build dependencies, and cache checks.

output_examples.input: Review an Abilities API pull request before merge.
output_examples.output: A review summary covering stable IDs, schemas, permissions, REST exposure, client usage, and missing test coverage.

best_practices: Register categories before abilities with the documented init hooks.
Use stable namespaced ability IDs, schemas, and permission callbacks.
Expose only needed abilities through REST and verify responses in WordPress.
anti_patterns: Do not register abilities outside the Abilities API init hook.
Do not expose write-capable abilities to REST without permission checks.
Do not change ability IDs after clients depend on them.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps implement, expose, consume, and debug WordPress Abilities API features in plugins, themes, and core work.

faq.question: Does it write code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides agent guidance for code changes, but the agent still edits files in the user workspace.

faq.question: Which WordPress version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets WordPress 6.9 and later. Older projects may need the separate Abilities API package or plugin.

faq.question: Can it help with REST visibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks endpoint availability, show_in_rest settings, and ability or category presence in REST responses.

faq.question: Does it cover permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends permission callbacks for abilities that modify data or expose sensitive information.

faq.question: Can frontend developers use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It points agents toward @wordpress/abilities and build pipeline checks for client-side usage.
